The bill would update Australia's space laws to keep pace with changes in the industry.
It expands the rules to cover launches from aircraft and high-power rockets, and simplifies approvals and insurance.
Insurance for each launch or return would be capped at $100 million, down from the previous minimum of $750 million, set in rules Parliament can disallow.

Reduces barriers to entry by streamlining approval processes and insurance requirements.

The Space Activities Amendment (Launches and Returns) Bill 2018 reduces red tape, streamlines approvals and insurance requirements for space launches and returns, and introduces licensing for launches from aircraft, aiming to boost Australia's 0.8% share of the global space sector (worth over US$345 billion) and support innovation, investment and job creation.
